This is an ___ gentleman who has a past medical history 
of known CAD s/p CABG (LIMA-LAD; SVG-OM1; SVG-PDA) in ___, 
multiple prior PCI's, Afib on coumadin, hypertension, 
hyperlipidemia, and diet controlled diabetes, who presented with 
substernal chest pain, and EKG changes concerning for an NSTEMI.

# NSTEMI: The patient was admitted with a troponin of 1.32 that 
peaked at 2.2.
He was started on aspirin 325 mg and loaded with
600 mg of clopidogrel.

Heparin was held because the patient had 
an INR of 2.8 on admission.

The patient had no chest pain on 
admission and an ECG that was only significant for 1 mm
ST-segment elevation in aVR, and possible lateral lead ischemia.

He underwent cardiac 
catheterization, which showed no new coronary lesions.
His

NSTEMI was attributed to demand ischemia from anemia in the 
setting of existing coronary artery disease.
# Anemia: Pt had hematocrit of 28.7 on admission that fell to
24.7 overnight.

On physical exam, he had a large hematoma on the 
right side of his back.

CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis 
demonstrated rib fractures as the cause of the hematoma.

No RP 
bleed was identified.

He received two units of pRBCs to replete 
his hematocrit.

He responded appropriately and did not show any 
signs of further blood loss.

# Hyponatremia: Pt had sodium of 126 on admission that reached a 
nadir of 122 during his hospitalization.

The patient was 
euvolemic and had a urine osmolality of 400, suggesting the 
syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone secretion.

This 
was believed to be a result of his rib fractures.

He was fluid 
restricted and sodium trended upward, reaching a peak of 132 by 
discharge.

# Systolic heart failure: The patient had an echo to evaluate 
his left ventricular function following his MI.

It demonstrated 
an ejection fraction of 30 - 35%, which was significantly 
decreased from his last echo where his EF was 40 - 45%.

However, 
he did not have any signs of acute decompensation of his chronic 
heart failure and remained euvolemic during his hospitilization.
He was medically managed as described above.

# Rhythm: The patient was in normal sinus rhythm during his 
hospitilzation.

He is on warfarin chronically secondary to a 
history of atrial fibrillation.

His INR on admission was 2.8, 
which fell to 1.5 by his catheterization.

After cath, he was 
anticoagulated in the hospital with subcutaneous heparin.
Warfarin was withheld to prevent recurrence of his bleeding.

The 
warfarin will not be started again at the time of discharge.
Dr.

We therefore changed his 
aspirin from 81 mg daily to 325 mg daily.

We also started 
clopidogrel 75 mg daily to serve as an alternative in stroke 
prevention.

# Diabetes: The patient's diabetes was controlled with an 
insulin sliding scale.

Blood glucose checks were within or 
better than a target range of 140 - 170.

# History of falls: The patient was placed under fall 
precautions as he was at high risk for a fall.

He is not stable 
to ambulate independently and requires assistance.
